This 5 in 1 hub has been extremely helpful for some of my everyday tasks at work. It is super reliable and simple to use. It's small and compact so it's easy to store and packs away with my laptop. Macs have very few connecting ports so this is vital. I have to set up MP3 players with music and this has made it so easy. It's simple to connect and quick to use. If you've ever wanted to mirror your laptop screen to a TV, this is the answer as well. You literally just plug it into the USB-C port and then you can plug in multiple devices. This $30 device has made so many tasks possible. It does whatever I throw at it. It's high quality and definitely a good value. I definitely recommend it. (Amazon Vine review — reviewer received the product free.)

This 5-in-1 hub solves the immediate problem of running out of USB ports, with a detachable 20-inch cable that's a perfect length, reinforced port ends that feel strong, and the convenience of seeing what you're charging at a glance. The packaging is nice and if you need basic connectivity — connecting your MacBook to a TV, running a simple slideshow from a thumb drive, or charging while doing light tasks — this will get the job done. Where the "Pro Series" branding falls apart: the title mentions Thunderbolt 3/4, which is misleading, because a true Thunderbolt device would offer significantly higher bandwidth; what you actually get are two USB 2.0 ports and one "high-speed" USB 3.0 port that isn't particularly fast. If you work with large files, multiple storage devices, photos, videos, or backups, this hub is too limited. The detachable cable is genuinely nice, but overall the value isn't great for the price when better options exist. (Amazon Vine review — reviewer received the product free.)

This EZQuest hub is compact but delivers great performance. The 4K60 HDMI output works flawlessly, and the 100W PD passthrough keeps a laptop charged while using peripherals. The detachable cable is a nice touch for portability, and the USB 3.0 port provides fast data transfer. A dependable travel-friendly hub for MacBook, iPad, or Windows devices. (Amazon Vine review — reviewer received the product free.)

The packaging is really nice and gives the impression of a quality product. The item itself is all plastic and quite light; the cable is decent. However, the title is misleading — it's marketed as a "Pro Series" but it's essentially an entry-level laptop hub, and it mentions Thunderbolt, which is misleading (a true Thunderbolt 3/4 device would offer significantly higher bandwidth). The two USB 2.0 ports are a major drawback — fine for a keyboard or printer, and that's about it — and the single "high-speed" USB 3.0 port isn't particularly fast. If you work with data (large files, multiple storage devices, photos, videos, backups), this hub won't cut it. It works fine for basic connectivity: connect your MacBook to a TV, run a simple slideshow from a thumb drive, and charge at the same time. The detachable cable is a nice feature that not many hubs offer — I'll give it that — but overall the value isn't great; there are better options in this price range. (Amazon Vine review — reviewer received the product free.)

I picked this up because my newer laptop has fully moved on from USB-A, and I still have plenty of devices that rely on it. The standout feature for me is the detachable USB-C cable — I've had other hubs where the fixed cable eventually became the weak point. Being able to disconnect it makes this much easier to pack and gives more flexibility in how you position the hub. Port selection is good: you get three USB-A ports, and I like that they clearly label the speeds so you know which one to use for faster devices. HDMI worked great with an external display, and power delivery worked as expected. That said, I do wish it had at least one additional USB-C data port. Build quality feels good — lightweight but not flimsy, and reliable with no disconnects. A practical, no-drama hub that does exactly what it should. Pros: detachable cable, clearly labeled USB speeds, reliable HDMI, working power delivery, compact. Cons: no additional USB-C data ports, limited port selection vs larger hubs. (Amazon Vine review — reviewer received the product free.)

With many laptops and devices ditching all non-USB-C ports these days, a hub is handy — and this one takes it further. Where most portable hubs have a fixed, short pigtail cable that gets in the way, this hub has a removable USB-C host cable. That makes it easier to pack, more durable (those cable ends are a weak point), and more flexible (use a short cable or a longer one to position the hub near power or a screen). Port-wise you get HDMI up to 4K/60Hz, two 480Mbps USB-A ports great for keyboards/mice/controllers, one 5Gbps USB-A port for a drive, and USB-C for power delivery up to 100W (passing up to 80W to the host). The hub is well-built with mostly metal construction and the ports are clearly labeled. If you're in the market for a nice portable hub for your USB-C devices, this could be just what you're looking for. (Amazon Vine review — reviewer received the product free.)

A good little addition when you have an older laptop with only the previous type of USB port. It fits the bill and I'm getting some use out of it. Love the look and color, and the length of the cable is just right. (Amazon Vine review — reviewer received the product free.)

This is like having a power strip for your USB ports. I cannot rave about this product enough. The port ends are reinforced with very thick, super strong sections where the wire would bend, to prevent splits. If you're anything like me you're probably out of available USB ports — this device solves that problem, and you can see what you're charging or using at a quick glance without turning your computer around. The cord is strong and thick and a perfect length — not too long, not too short. It even has high-speed pass-through charging. Highly recommend. (Amazon Vine review — reviewer received the product free.)

The hub has worked well. It passes power from my laptop charger through to my laptop, outputs to an external monitor, and operates a wired mouse with no issues. The detachable host cable feels solid and lets you use a longer or shorter cable. I've also used it as a secondary hub connected to my primary work hub — it works for USB devices, though in my case not for an additional monitor. One possible negative: on Windows 11 on my Lenovo ThinkPad, a warning notification pops up every few minutes (it doesn't affect operation and doesn't happen on my Dell). It's also very light, which gives an impression of cheapness, but it does what it's supposed to do effectively. (Amazon Vine review — reviewer received the product free.)

This is a lightweight, compact USB hub that extends the ports on your laptop. It includes an HDMI port, a USB-C port and 3 USB-A ports that handle different data transfer speeds. It would have been nice to include an extra USB-C port instead of 3 USB-A ports, since the one USB-C port pretty much just replaces the one you plugged into on your laptop. (Amazon Vine review — reviewer received the product free.)

I picked up this EZQuest 5-in-1 hub to simplify my setup and avoid constantly plugging and unplugging devices, and it's been exactly what I needed. It turns a single USB-C port into a much more usable workstation with HDMI, USB ports, and power delivery. The 4K@60Hz HDMI output works cleanly with no flickering or resolution drops. Build quality feels solid, and I really like the detachable cable design. It's compact enough to throw in a bag but durable for daily use. Data transfer speeds have been consistent, and the 100W power delivery passthrough keeps my laptop charged. It doesn't overload you with ports you won't use — just the essentials, and they all work well together. If you need Ethernet or an SD card reader you'll want something more advanced, but as a clean, dependable USB-C hub it does exactly what I expect. (Amazon Vine review — reviewer received the product free.)

This hub is exactly what I needed for my setup. The 4K 60Hz HDMI output is noticeably smoother than standard 30Hz adapters, great for video editing or high-res content. The 100W Power Delivery charges my laptop quickly even with multiple peripherals plugged in. The 20-inch detachable cable is a game-changer — plenty of flexibility to keep the hub tucked away and my desk clean. It feels high-quality and works seamlessly with both my MacBook and iPad. Highly recommended for anyone who needs a reliable, high-performance multiport adapter! (Amazon Vine review — reviewer received the product free.)

I had an immediate use for this type of USB hub. It can power my mini-PC with the proper USB-to-barrel adapter, and has 3 USB-A ports, an additional USB-C port and HDMI. I recently reconfigured my desk layout and this was exactly what I needed. The 20-inch separate cable is a nice extra instead of the short pre-attached cables of other hubs. I like the solid, sturdy feel of the hub and data speed is up to spec. A good value at its current discounted price. Nice additions for an upgraded version would be an SD card slot and an Ethernet port. (Amazon Vine review — reviewer received the product free.)

I have a Surface Go, which only has a single USB-C port, and wanted to extend its life. While the hub works without a power adapter if you only need the extra ports, I needed one in my case — I used a 65W power adapter (not included) and it handles power delivery to the laptop without issues. After plugging a monitor, keyboard and mouse into it and installing Ubuntu from a USB drive, my Surface Go is ready to roll. I like that it uses a detachable USB-C cable, which allows a longer cable if necessary. (Amazon Vine review — reviewer received the product free.)

This 5-in-1 hub is great. I had one I used for a long time but needed a new one. The cord that plugs in is wrapped for better protection of the cable. You can easily use all the ports, and transfers are fast. The cord isn't super long, but a decent distance — not too long and not too short. The hub feels sturdy in my hands. I use it a lot for my MacBook Pro since it only has a USB-C port. (Amazon Vine review — reviewer received the product free.)

I've needed a powered hub for my computer because my motherboard doesn't behave well with too many USBs plugged in — this seems to have solved that issue. The other additions are nice and I've used them a bunch already; the HDMI is becoming a daily use to extend my desktop. It's solid and well built and sturdy — I've thrown it in my bag 100 times already and there's nary a scratch on it. For the price point, I like it and can happily recommend. (Amazon Vine review — reviewer received the product free.)

Nice hub. It's very small and compact and the white makes it a nice travel piece. It's got some weight to it, which makes me feel like it might be more durable than my mostly-plastic one. (Amazon Vine review — reviewer received the product free.)
This is exactly what I needed for my MacBook to see items saved on USB flash drives. (Amazon Vine review — reviewer received the product free.)

I have several small external drives I use with my laptop and this item is a huge help. I can use the one port on my laptop to extend it to a pass-through USB-C port, 3 regular USB ports and one HDMI if needed. It packs a lot of use into one very slim, efficient small unit. Perfect for laptops that use multiple outputs, and it can also charge 3 devices. (Amazon Vine review — reviewer received the product free.)

We took this EZQuest 5-in-1 hub with us on a camping trip because my daughter wanted to try playing videos on her new projector. We used it to stream video from an HP laptop to the projector and it helped reduce the lag. It has ports for every type of connection that may be needed. It worked very well. (Amazon Vine review — reviewer received the product free.)
